transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-06-18
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~47 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Marco Diaz (Redwood SE), Priya Singh (Redwood SE), Sophie Lin (MarketBridge PM), Ravi Patel (MarketBridge Eng Lead), Tom O'Neil (MarketBridge Security), Aisha Hassan (MarketBridge Product)

Summary: Quick partner technical sync to go over listing requirements for MarketBridge marketplace, design of reference architecture for customers that will use Redwood Private via VPC, SSO and KMS integration points, and action items for pilot listing. Some audio / transcription glitches; names may be slightly off in places.

00:00 - Lena Park: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you slotting time for this. We'll run through checklist, reference arch, and any blockers for the marketplace listing. I'm Lena, I'll coordinate the next steps.
00:22 - Sophie Lin: Hi Lena, thanks, yeah excited. I'll hand over to Ravi for the infra details then Tom for security.
00:30 - Ravi Patel: Hey all, quick context — MarketBridge wants to offer Redwood as a first-class marketplace listing, customers should be able to provision either hosted API or a private deployment via our marketplace UI. Key ask is: how do we package the private option, and what artifacts do you need from Redwood.
00:55 - Marco Diaz: Cool. So from Redwood side we generally have two flows: hosted (our API) and private (VPC/on-prem). For marketplace listings you typically need an AMI/container image reference, reference architecture diagram, a small install guide, and SSO/KMS notes. Also, we'll need a listing metadata sheet — model names, consumption metrics, and sample pricing guidance.
01:20 - Sophie Lin: For the private flow customers expect a one-click-ish experience via our provisioning. How much automation can Redwood provide?
01:35 - Priya Singh: We can provide a deployable artifact — container image + helm chart — and a config repo. For truly one-click provisioning we'd need to collaborate on the marketplace side to wire up secrets (K S M credentials) and networking. There may be some manual steps for dedicated infra mapping.
01:50 - Tom O'Neil: On security, our buyers require SOC 2, audit logs, and SAML SSO. What does Redwood expose for audit logs and KMS integration?
02:05 - Marco Diaz: We support KMS/HSM integration; we can accept customer-managed keys for private deployments. Audit logs are available via our console and we can stream them to S3 or a syslog endpoint. Small caveat — the log retention policy is configurable but if the marketplace requires a specific retention we need to agree on retention window.
02:30 - Ravi Patel: Also routing policy — if a customer chooses hosted vs private at purchase time, do we have a fallback? e.g., if capacity isn't available in Redwood Dedicated pools.
02:45 - Lena Park: Good question. We can surface routing policies but fallbacks are an operational policy. For marketplace we can list recommended SLOs and a fallback option to hosted API; we should document that.
03:05 - Sophie Lin: Ok that's helpful. On billing — customers will want the cost broken down (Redwood usage vs marketplace fee). Any standard approach?
03:20 - Marco Diaz: Common approach is to meter tokens/embedding units in the listing metadata and denote billing lines. If MarketBridge needs us to push usage to your billing system we can support a usage export. There is sometimes a delay of 24h in usage export depending on batching.
03:40 - Aisha Hassan: For the reference architecture — we'd like a diagram that shows the VPC peering, SSO handshake, KMS flow, and where the data residency controls sit.
03:55 - Priya Singh: We'll draft a canonical diagram showing MarketBridge customer VPC <-> Redwood Private, peering via Transit Gateway (or direct connect), SAML IdP flow from MarketBridge to customer IdP to Redwood, and key management arrows — KMS in customer account used to encrypt model keys.
04:20 - Tom O'Neil: Are there any special network ports or egress requirements we should call out?
04:30 - Marco Diaz: Standard HTTPs for the control plane and gRPC for inference in some cases; we can provide a minimal ports list. Also note that the KV cache is local to the instance — sometimes docs call it 'K V cash' in transcripts — but that's internal caching.
04:55 - Ravi Patel: For the marketplace listing assets — screenshots, quickstart, and a sandbox credential set, do you provide test keys we can use in staging?
05:10 - Lena Park: Yes we can provide a staging API key and a small sandbox deployment manifest. We'll need a MarketBridge staging environment for the private flow so the provisioning hook can be exercised.
05:25 - Sophie Lin: On legal/compliance, we'll need your SOC2 cert and a security questionnaire completed. We'll share the exact questionnaire, but is SOC2 Type II available?
05:40 - Marco Diaz: Yes, SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 — we'll attach those certs and an infosec contact. There may be some names mis-transcribed in the notes but we'll send the official docs.
06:00 - Sophie Lin: Great. Next — timeline. We are aiming to have a beta listing by end of July. Is that feasible?
06:12 - Lena Park: End of July is tight but doable if we keep a steady tempo. Key milestones: reference arch by 6/25, compatibility test by 6/24, marketplace asset bundle by 6/20, and legal onboarding parallel.
06:30 - Sophie Lin: Sounds reasonable. Any technical blockers?
06:35 - Marco Diaz: Nothing blocking on our side. We do need to validate that the helm chart supports the Marketplace's provisioning hooks — some marketplaces expect a specific return payload after provisioning. We'll need to review MarketBridge's provisioning webhook spec.
06:55 - Ravi Patel: We'll send that spec after the call.
07:02 - Priya Singh: Also a note on model packaging — if MarketBridge wants to include a curated model list in the listing, we should include the model catalog and recommended quantization for cost. That way customers see recommended cost-performance tradeoffs.
07:25 - Aisha Hassan: Yes, we'd like to surface a few suggestions in the listing copy.
07:35 - Marco Diaz: We'll share a recommended profile file: model names, expected latency at 512 tokens, and a recommended quantized variant.
07:50 - Tom O'Neil: From security — SAML metadata exchange and certificate rotation are concerns. How do you recommend cert rotation be handled for long-lived marketplace deployments?
08:05 - Priya Singh: We recommend short-lived certs for service-to-service tokens and an automated rotation in the customer's KMS; for SAML assertions you can have a metadata refresh schedule. We'll document recommended rotation cadence.
08:25 - Sophie Lin: Does Redwood support SCIM for user provisioning from MarketBridge?
08:30 - Marco Diaz: SCIM is supported in our hosted console but for private deployments it's up to the customer to host SCIM or use a connector we can provide. We'll note that as a capability matrix item.
08:50 - Lena Park: Quick pivot — joint collateral. MarketBridge wants a co-branded launch doc and a technical blog. Who owns what?
09:05 - Sophie Lin: MarketBridge can write the marketplace announcement and we can do a joint technical blog. We'll need a short technical blurb from Redwood and a reference architecture diagram.
09:20 - Marco Diaz: Redwood can draft the technical blurb and the reference diagram; we'll hand over a draft for your PR team to review.
09:35 - Ravi Patel: For the pilot, can we do a joint-run of a demo provisioning where MarketBridge provisions a private deployment into a test account and we validate connectivity?
09:50 - Priya Singh: Yes, that's the plan. Priya will run the smoke test and confirm the private deploy flow.
10:00 - Sophie Lin: Good. Action item notes here: Marco diagram, Lena checklist, Priya smoke test.
10:10 - Marco Diaz: Also need to align on billing metering: do you want per-token billing or a seat-based? MarketBridge typically prefers usage-based but can do a hybrid.
10:25 - Aisha Hassan: We'll probably launch with usage-based billing and an option to bundle a service fee. We'll confirm with finance and get back.
10:40 - Tom O'Neil: One more security note — customers ask about model governance: can Redwood restrict model updates and provide eval snapshots?
10:55 - Marco Diaz: Yes, model pinning is supported; we can provide eval snapshots and quality monitoring for regressions. We'll include that in the collateral.
11:10 - Sophie Lin: Ok great. Any other integrations like Vault or HashiCorp?
11:18 - Marco Diaz: We have out-of-the-box docs for HashiCorp Vault integration for key retrieval; we can include that as an advanced integration appendix.
11:30 - Ravens — sorry mis-transcribe.
11:35 - Lena Park: (laughs) noted, we will clean transcript.
11:40 - Sophie Lin: Let's quickly walk through the marketplace checklist you mentioned.
11:45 - Marco Diaz: Checklist: 1) Artifact bundle (container image + helm chart + manifest), 2) Reference architecture diagram, 3) Security docs (SOC2/ISO/pen test summary), 4) SAML/SCIM/KMS integration notes, 5) Billing/usage export spec, 6) Demo provisioning hook spec, 7) Screenshots and marketing blurbs, 8) Support contact and escalation path.
12:20 - Ravi Patel: That's comprehensive. For item 1, what image registry do you prefer? ECR or GCR?
12:30 - Marco Diaz: ECR is our default for customers on AWS, but we can provide images in GCR if you need GCP-native. We'll produce a small matrix in the assets doc.
12:45 - Sophie Lin: For the demo, can we have a short recorded walkthrough as well as live?
12:50 - Priya Singh: Yes, we'll record a 5–7 minute walkthrough of provisioning hosted + private via MarketBridge staging and attach it to the assets.
13:10 - Tom O'Neil: Regarding audits — customers sometimes ask for penetration test reports. We can't share full reports but can provide a summary + contact for deeper discussions under NDA.
13:25 - Marco Diaz: Agreed, we have a summary and can do an NDA exchange for full docs.
13:40 - Lena Park: OK great, let's call out deadlines — Marco, can you do the reference arch by 6/25?
13:48 - Marco Diaz: Yes, I can.
13:50 - Lena Park: Priya, compatibility smoke test by 6/24?
13:53 - Priya Singh: Yup, will do.
13:55 - Lena Park: Sophie, you'll provide the provisioning webhook spec after this call?
13:58 - Sophie Lin: Yes, I'll send the spec and the legal questionnaire.
14:05 - Sophie Lin: One small question — do you have any concerns about model licensing in a marketplace context?
14:12 - Marco Diaz: We need to ensure the model licenses are compatible with redistribution via a marketplace. Most of our curated models are open license or Redwood-managed; for third-party models we will surface license info in the listing.
14:30 - Ravi Patel: Thanks.
14:35 - Aisha Hassan: On launch plan — we'd like to aim for an early adopter cohort of 5 customers. We will coordinate outreach.
14:45 - Lena Park: Sounds good.
14:50 - Marco Diaz: Quick note — for private deployments, we may recommend a quantized model variant for cost reasons; we'll provide guidance per workload.
15:05 - Sophie Lin: Good call.
15:10 - Tom O'Neil: Anything on the support side — what is Redwood's recommended SLA for marketplace customers?
15:18 - Marco Diaz: For hosted customers we typically offer a baseline SLO; for Marketplace we can recommend a tier: self-serve (no SLA), standard (4hr response), premium (SLA with dedicated on-call). We'll include recommended language.
15:35 - Sophie Lin: Ok, final recap then next steps.
15:40 - Lena Park: Recap: Marco will produce reference architecture diagram (due 6/25). Priya will run compatibility smoke tests and report (due 6/24). Lena will share marketplace checklist and pricing template (due 6/20). Sophie to send provisioning webhook spec and legal questionnaire (due 6/20). Redwood to provide staging keys and sandbox artifacts. We'll schedule follow-up demo week of 6/30.
16:10 - Sophie Lin: That matches our notes, thanks.
16:20 - Ravi Patel: Thanks everyone, we'll look for the docs.
16:28 - Lena Park: Thanks all, we'll follow up via email with links to the drive and action items.
16:35 - (call ends)
